site.name: Akeem

welcome.line: hi, i'm akeem. i build products people actually use.

site.statement: I’m Akeem, a full-stack PERN developer — PostgreSQL, Express, React, Node. I take an idea all the way to a live URL: the interface, the API behind it, the database under that, and the deploy.
site.workIntro: Products built and shipped end to end. Real sites, recorded live.

now.label: Currently building
now.text: Turning ideas into useful digital products.

engineering.headline: One click. *Everything it wakes up.*
engineering.intro: Every action runs through the same stack my products are built on. Watch what you’d see, what the server sees, and where each millisecond goes. Or press the button and run it yourself.

about.headline: Full-stack, from first commit *to live URL.*

blocks.label: What I build
blocks.text: Web products, start to finish. The interface people touch, the API it talks to, the database underneath, and the deploy that puts it online.

blocks.label: How I work
blocks.text: Ship something real early, then improve it in public. Every project on this page is live, and every one of them is still getting better.

blocks.label: What I care about
blocks.text: Pages that respond the moment you touch them. Data models that still make sense a year later. Code someone else can read.

headline: Good ideas deserve
*to be built.*
contact.note: Email is the quickest way to reach me.

hero.headline: Real products, *live right now.*
hero.sub: A stock-market school, a software review site, a shopping guide, a leisure complex’s bookings and an artist’s site — each one designed, built and launched by me. Tap one to watch it run.

story.idea: A shop that tells you who each product is actually for.

chapters.title: It starts with *an idea.*
chapters.text: A problem someone keeps running into. For KeemStore: shopping sites that never say who a product is really for.

chapters.title: I design *how it looks.*
chapters.text: Every screen, colour and button — so anyone can use it without thinking.

chapters.title: I build what *you never see.*
chapters.text: Behind every page there’s a brain that makes decisions and a memory that keeps everything safe. Tap a button, and all three work together in a blink.

chapters.title: I put it *live.*
chapters.text: On a real web address — fast, secure, and open to anyone, anywhere.

chapters.title: And people *use it.*
chapters.text: This is the real KeemStore, recorded live. Not a mockup.

problems.headline: Every product started as *a frustration.*
problems.intro: Before the code, there was something annoying, broken or missing. Here’s what each one fixed.

projects.contribution: Designed and built it alone: the React front end, the Express API behind tools, categories and promotion, the PostgreSQL data through Prisma, and the deploy on Vercel and Render.

anatomy.name: The experience
anatomy.text: I built it around one question: which tool should I pick? Browsing, head-to-head comparison, curated stacks and the way a maker submits a tool each get their own page.

anatomy.name: Frontend
anatomy.text: React and Vite, shipped as a single-page app, so moving between tools and guides feels instant.

anatomy.name: API
anatomy.text: A Node and Express API serves the catalogue. Promoted tools come from their own endpoint, apart from the main tool list.

anatomy.name: Data
anatomy.text: Tools, reviews and guides live in PostgreSQL, reached through Prisma.

anatomy.name: Hosting
anatomy.text: The site runs on Vercel and the API on Render, so each can be deployed on its own.

showcase.headline: I wanted a better way to discover software. So I built one.
showcase.text: I built Toolhaven as an independent index of software. Every review says what the tool is bad at, paid placements stay out of the rankings, and prices come from the vendor’s own page.
showcase.highlight: Paid placements are labelled and never touch the rankings

projects.title: Toolhaven
projects.headline: Finding the right tool shouldn’t cost you a week of open tabs.
projects.description: An independent index of software tools. Every review lists what the tool is bad at, paid placements are labelled and kept apart from rankings, and prices come from the vendor’s own page.
projects.why: I wanted to make product discovery feel less like scrolling through another directory.
projects.whatIBuilt: A discovery platform with submissions, reviews, monetization and editorial content.
features: A searchable tool index, with ⌘K search from anywhere
Reviews that always list the downsides
Put three tools head to head
Buying guides and curated stacks
Reader reviews and ratings
Paid placements labelled and kept out of the rankings
Night mode

image.alt: Toolhaven home page: “Finding the right tool shouldn’t cost you a week of open tabs.” with a search bar.

projects.plain: A website that reviews software honestly — downsides included.
projects.hook: Most “best tools” lists are ads in disguise. Toolhaven shows you where the money is — and keeps it out of the rankings.

highlights.title: Downsides on every review
highlights.benefit: You learn what a tool is bad at before you pay for it, not after.

highlights.title: Paid placements labelled, kept out of rankings
highlights.benefit: Sponsors can’t buy their way up, so the order means something.

highlights.title: Three tools, head to head
highlights.benefit: Compare your shortlist side by side instead of juggling ten tabs.

highlights.title: Prices from the vendor’s own page
highlights.benefit: The number you see is the number you’ll actually be charged.

highlights.title: ⌘K search from anywhere
highlights.benefit: Jump to any tool from any page without losing your place.

highlights.title: Buying guides and curated stacks
highlights.benefit: Start from a proven set of tools for the job, not a blank search box.

problem.headline: Finding the right tool took a week of open tabs.
problem.text: Thousands of tools, and almost every “review” is quietly an ad. People ended up comparing sponsored lists that never mention a single downside.
problem.solution: An independent index where every review lists what the tool is bad at, paid placements are labelled and kept out of the rankings, and prices come from the vendor’s own page.

projects.contribution: Designed and built the whole platform: courses, the practice simulator, rankings and the forum in React, with an Express API and PostgreSQL behind accounts and the practice market.

anatomy.name: Frontend

anatomy.name: API

anatomy.name: Data

showcase.headline: Making the stock market easier to understand.
showcase.text: I built StockAcademia so a beginner can start from zero, practise with pretend money, and get any US or Nigerian stock explained in plain language.
showcase.highlight: Explanations in English, Pidgin, Yorùbá, Hausa and Igbo

projects.title: StockAcademia
projects.headline: Learn how the stock market really works — from zero to confident investor.
projects.description: An AI that analyses any US or Nigerian stock in plain English, turns it into a clear plan and keeps watching it for you — plus a place to learn investing properly: structured courses from “what’s a dividend?” upward, a practice account to trade without risking real money, and plain-language explanations of US and Nigerian stocks — in English, Pidgin, Yorùbá, Hausa and Igbo.
features: AI Stock Scout: scans US and Nigerian stocks for potential setups, ranked to your profile
Plain-English AI analysis with a potential entry, stop and targets
Keeps watching and alerts you when something important changes
Six structured courses, from the basics to technical analysis
A $100,000 practice account — learn without risking real money
US and Nigerian (NGX) stocks, side by side
Explanations in English, Pidgin, Yorùbá, Hausa and Igbo
The numbers that matter — P/E, ROE, margins — explained simply
1-on-1 mentorship and a community forum

image.alt: StockAcademia home page: “Any stock, analysed. Then watched for you.”

gallery.caption: From first search to final review

projects.plain: A platform that teaches people how the stock market works — from zero to confident investor.
projects.hook: Any stock, analysed — then watched for you. And $100,000 of practice money to learn with, at no risk.

highlights.title: AI Stock Scout
highlights.benefit: Scans US and Nigerian stocks for potential setups and ranks the ones that fit your profile — no more scrolling charts for ideas.

highlights.title: Plain-English analysis with a clear plan
highlights.benefit: Every analysis ends in a potential entry, stop and targets, so you know where you’d be wrong before you buy.

highlights.title: It keeps watching, and alerts you
highlights.benefit: When something important changes you get an alert — no endless feed, no staring at charts all day.

highlights.title: A $100,000 practice account
highlights.benefit: Make your first trades — and your first mistakes — without risking real money.

highlights.title: Five languages, including Pidgin, Yorùbá, Hausa and Igbo
highlights.benefit: Learn the market in the language you actually think in.

highlights.title: US and Nigerian (NGX) stocks side by side
highlights.benefit: Study the companies you know, not only Wall Street.

highlights.title: Six structured courses
highlights.benefit: A clear path from “what’s a dividend?” to technical analysis, in the right order.

highlights.title: 1-on-1 mentorship and a community forum
highlights.benefit: When a lesson isn’t enough, a real person and other learners are there.

problem.headline: Investing was taught in jargon — and learned with real money.
problem.text: P/E, ROE, margins: words that mean nothing until someone explains them. Most material assumed US markets and English, and beginners learned by losing money.
problem.solution: Courses that start from zero, a practice account with $100,000 of pretend money, and the real numbers explained simply — for US and Nigerian stocks, in five languages.

highlights.title: A “who it’s for” note on every product
highlights.benefit: Know whether something suits you before you click buy.

highlights.title: Buying guides that say what to skip
highlights.benefit: Save money on the things that aren’t worth it.

highlights.title: Browse by room, person or problem

highlights.title: Trending finds, refreshed through the season

problem.headline: Shopping online meant endless scrolling — and still guessing.
problem.text: Thousands of near-identical products, and nothing that tells you who a thing is actually for. You scroll, compare, and hope.
problem.solution: A curated guide: fewer, better finds — each with an honest note on who it suits and who should skip it — plus buying guides that say what not to buy.
fixes: A “who it’s for” note on every pick
Guides that say what to skip

projects.contribution: Designed and built the bookings site end to end: four ways to book, the live board, Google sign-in, and the Express API on PostgreSQL.

anatomy.name: The experience
anatomy.text: Five spaces, four ways in. I made each one behave the way it works in real life, instead of forcing everything through one booking form.

anatomy.name: Frontend
anatomy.text: React and Vite, with Google sign-in, and a phone layout with its own bottom navigation.

anatomy.name: API
anatomy.text: An Express API. The live board has its own endpoint, and rooms and the lounge menu hang off their facility.

anatomy.name: Data
anatomy.text: PostgreSQL. Every facility record carries its own booking mode, which is how the site knows how each space should be booked.

anatomy.name: Hosting
anatomy.text: The site runs on Vercel and the API on Render.

showcase.headline: One venue. Four ways to book.
showcase.text: I built the site for a leisure complex in Ibadan. A membership for the gym, dates for the hotel, slots for the pitch, and phone ordering at the lounge.
showcase.highlight: A live board showing what’s free right now

projects.title: Primetime
projects.headline: A gym, a hotel, a bar lounge and a football pitch in Ibadan — joined, booked and paid for in one place.
projects.description: The website for Primetime, a leisure complex in Ibadan. One membership covers the gym and table tennis; hotel rooms are booked by date, pitch slots by the hour, and the lounge needs no booking at all — you scan the code on your table and order from your phone. A live board shows what the complex is like right now.
features: A live “right now” board: how busy the gym is, pitch slots left, rooms free tonight
One membership for the gym, with table tennis included
Hotel rooms booked by date and held the moment you reserve
Football pitch slots checked for clashes as you book
Lounge ordering from your phone: scan the table code, order, settle the bill
Match nights listings
Google sign-in and a personal bookings dashboard

projects.plain: A website where people join, book and pay for a leisure complex: gym, hotel, football pitch and lounge.
projects.hook: Four parts of one venue, each booked a different way — and the site knows which is which.

highlights.title: See the complex before you leave home
highlights.benefit: A live board shows how busy the gym is, how many pitch slots are left and which rooms are free tonight.

highlights.title: One membership, the whole gym
highlights.benefit: Register once and train daily — table tennis comes free with it.

highlights.title: Rooms held the moment you reserve
highlights.benefit: Pick a room and your dates, pay per night, and nobody else can take it.

highlights.title: Pitch slots that can’t double-book
highlights.benefit: Availability is checked the second you book, so two teams never turn up for the same hour.

highlights.title: Order from your table
highlights.benefit: No waiting for a waiter: scan the code, order from your phone and settle the bill there.

highlights.title: Everything in one account
highlights.benefit: Sign in with Google and see every membership and booking in one dashboard.

problem.search: Calling to ask if the pitch is free
problem.headline: One venue, four ways to book — and all of them a phone call.
problem.text: A gym, a hotel, a football pitch and a lounge each work differently. Without one system, every membership, room and match slot means a call, a wait and a chance of two people booking the same thing.
problem.solution: One site that knows how each space works: a membership for the gym, dates for the hotel, slots for the pitch, and walk-in phone ordering for the lounge — with a live board showing what’s free right now.
fixes: Order from the table, no waiting

problem.headline: A performer’s best proof is the crowd — and it didn’t fit in a bio.
problem.text: Bookings came through DMs, one question at a time: are you free, how much, do you have videos? Nowhere showed the energy of a real night.
